answer: Run a pre-order test before launching: on planning assumptions a subscription would earn about [F11] a month, small next to [F12] from cafés, and it puts café accounts at risk.
exec_summary: Each café bag earns [F5]; a subscription bag would earn about [F8], but only on assumed prices and shipping costs.
Converting [F9] of the newsletter would mean about [F10] subscribers, an assumption until it is measured.
That would add about [F11] a month against [F12] a month from café sales today.
Two large cafés have already asked about being undercut, so channel conflict is a real cost.
situation: A specialty roaster selling [F1] bags a month to cafés, with no online sales yet.
complication: A subscription could earn more per bag, but the numbers that decide it have never been measured, and cafés are wary.
key_question: Should the roaster launch a direct-to-consumer subscription next year?
